executive_summary: EUR/CAD trades at 1.60356 as of the price payload's spot date of 2026-09-03, meaning one euro buys 1.60356 Canadian dollars, and the pair has gone almost nowhere for a year: down 0.95% over one month, down 0.36% over three, up 1.99% over six and down 1.62% over twelve, leaving spot at the 48th percentile of its 52-week closing range of 1.56817-1.64218. This is the zero-carry cross - the ECB deposit facility rate and the Bank of Canada overnight target both sit at 2.25%, an exact 0bp policy differential that exists nowhere else in either dossier's benchmarking set - so the pair prices euro-area versus Canadian fundamentals with no rates overlay and, at 2.99% twenty-day realised volatility and a 55-pip ATR(14), it prices them slowly. The dominant bilateral narrative is a collision between two large and opposite forces: a rate and reaction-function divergence in which the market prices roughly 65% of a 2026 Bank of Canada hike that the Bank's own Q2 Market Participants Survey does not reach until March 2027, against a terms-of-trade shock in which the euro area is the world's largest net energy importer buying into an effectively closed Strait of Hormuz while Canada sells into it with energy explicitly carved out of the US tariff regime. Two differentials diverge sharply from what either standalone dossier would suggest - first, the Canadian speculative short is roughly nine times more crowded per unit of open interest than the euro's (39.8% of 329,544 contracts against 4.5% of 801,884), which flips the naive both legs short, signal muted reading into a genuine pair headwind; second, on relative BIS real effective exchange rates the euro is 7.3% rich to the Canadian dollar (102.69 against 95.71), so the cross is expensive at exactly the moment its fundamental case is improving. The settled direction is tactically Neutral at conviction 2 (net weighted score +0.0986, fourteen ten-thousandths short of the Bullish threshold) and strategically Bullish at conviction 2 (+0.1026, twenty-six ten-thousandths beyond it). The caveat, and it is a real one: the chart now available to this pass does not corroborate the strategic call - spot sits below the 50-, 100- and 200-day averages, has made lower highs since 5 August and a marginal lower low on 3 September, and the pair sold off 67 pips with a 113-pip range on the day of the Bank of Canada decision, the widest session in a month. The direction verdict stands as issued and is not re-scored here, but the price structure argues that the strategic thesis needs the 2026-10-28 Bank of Canada Monetary Policy Report to arrive before it earns its entry, not before.

market_context.valuation_assessment: There is no pair-level PPP series for EUR/CAD, so the valuation read is built from BIS real effective exchange rates for June 2026, both 63 days stale and breaching the 60-day strategic freshness window. The euro's broad real effective rate is 102.69 and Canada's is 95.71, putting EUR/CAD 7.3% rich on a relative real-effective basis - the euro near its BIS base period while the Canadian dollar is the second-cheapest currency in the eleven-currency set behind the yen, 4.29% below its own index base and down 3.41 points over twelve months. The euro's real rate fell 1.20 points over a year while Canada's fell 3.41, so the cross has been cheapening slowly even as the nominal rate held a range. This is the clearest valuation argument against the strategic Bullish - a structural level, not a catalyst, that caps the upside case: a move to the 1.6480 strategic upside target would push the relative gap toward 10%, where a valuation constraint starts to bind.

bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: The policy differential is exactly 0bp - the ECB deposit facility rate and the Bank of Canada overnight target both sit at 2.25% - making EUR/CAD the only zero-carry policy cross in either dossier's benchmarking set: a pure directional instrument on euro-area versus Canadian fundamentals with no rates overlay to help or hinder. The market-observable carry is not zero and it is negative: the listed-futures roll premium is -34.2bp annualised, observed 2026-08-31 over a 14.6-to-49.6-day window, consistent with a 45bp Canadian long-end advantage and Canadian three-month paper at 2.28% against euro-area ESTR near 2.05%. By covered interest parity that figure is the interest differential plus the cross-currency basis and cannot be separated without an OIS curve, so it must never be reported as a policy differential. Carry is working across G10 (VIX 14.51, US HY 263bp, equities at records) and EUR/CAD is the one place in either complex where it provides no support to either side, meaning this pair's direction has to be earned entirely on rate-of-change, terms of trade and event risk. A modest fundamental edge in a zero-carry, 2.99%-volatility instrument converts into a grind, not a move, which is the structural reason conviction is 2 at both horizons rather than 3.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The bilateral policy differential is exactly zero: the ECB deposit facility rate is 2.25% as of 2026-09-01 and the Bank of Canada overnight target is 2.25% as of 2026-08-31. That makes EUR/CAD the only zero-carry policy cross in either dossier's benchmarking set, and it means this factor cannot be scored on the level of the gap because there is no gap. The trajectory is euro-favourable and dated: the ECB decides on 2026-09-10 with a projections round attached, and euro-area OIS discounts a 25bp move to 2.50% at roughly 97%, which would open a +25bp euro advantage inside the tactical window. The Bank of Canada decided on 2026-09-02 with bond markets pricing a 3% hike probability and all 35 Reuters-polled economists forecasting no change. The problem for a tactical bull is that both legs are near-fully discounted, so neither meeting is a repricing event: a 97%-priced hike is an accounting entry, not a catalyst, and a 97%-priced hold is the same thing with the sign reversed. The long end runs the other way and is not priced out. Canada's 10-year yields 45bp more than the German benchmark on the payload's consistent monthly basis (3.42% versus 2.97%, both 2026-06-01), and the live levels agree almost exactly at roughly 44bp (Canada 3.74% against a Bund at 3.29-3.30% on 31 August). The market-observable cost of the position corroborates: the listed-futures roll premium is -34.2bp annualised, observed 2026-08-31 over a 14.6-to-49.6-day window, so a rolled long EUR/CAD pays roughly a third of a percent a year despite the identical policy rates. A zero policy gap, a negative funding carry and two fully discounted decisions is the definition of a Neutral rate factor over four weeks.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the two curves are priced for opposite errors, and both errors point the same way for this pair. On the euro leg the path is 2.25% now, 2.50% on 2026-09-10, with a further 25bp to 2.75% apparently discounted by early 2027; the base dossier's own view is that the terminal is 15-25bp too high because negotiated wages printed 2.1% in Q2 2026 against 3.2% in 2025. On the Canadian leg the market carries roughly a 65% probability of a Bank of Canada hike by end-2026, while the Bank's own Q2 2026 Market Participants Survey has the median policy rate at 2.25% through January 2027 and reaching 2.50% only in March 2027 - a one-to-two-quarter wedge. Both legs therefore face a downward repricing, but the Canadian one is larger, earlier and better evidenced: Canada's preferred core measures are CPI-trim at 1.9% and CPI-median at 2.0%, so the entire 100bp gap between 3.0% headline and target is gasoline at +25.7% year on year, whereas euro-area core sits at 2.5% with services at 3.3%. A central bank whose core is at target holds; a central bank whose core is half a point above it hikes. The dated anchor is the 2026-10-28 Bank of Canada decision with a Monetary Policy Report, which lands one day before the 2026-10-29 ECB decision - the Canadian projection round therefore sets the tone for the cross and is the meeting at which the Canadian hike premium most plausibly bleeds out. The second anchor is the pair of December meetings, 2026-12-09 for Canada and 2026-12-17 for the ECB with projections, in that order again. Direction of travel: the differential travels from 0bp toward +25bp and possibly +50bp in the euro's favour while the market currently prices some Canadian tightening. That is a genuine Bullish, capped at 55 confidence by the -34.2bp funding drag and by the fact that two of Canada's six largest banks forecast a hike.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both economies are running positive data-surprise sequences, which mutes the growth leg of this factor, but the inflation leg is genuinely divergent and it is the leg that transmits to the pair. Euro-area July HICP was 2.9% headline with HICPX core at 2.5% and services at 3.3%, the August flash consensus was 3.3% headline, and the already-released country prints ran hot - Spanish HICP 4.5% from 3.9%, French 2.7% from 2.4%, Belgian 3.97% from 3.56%. Canada's headline is comparable at 3.0% but its composition is the opposite: CPI-trim at 1.9% and CPI-median at 2.0% average exactly to target, CPI ex-gasoline has been pinned at 2.2% for three consecutive months, and gasoline at +25.7% year on year accounts for the entire overshoot. Wages complete the picture - Canadian wage growth decelerated to 2.8% from 3.3%, against euro-area services inflation still running at 3.3%. On activity the rearview favours Canada and the forward view does not: Canada printed 3.3% annualised in Q2 against a 2.5% Bank of Canada forecast with unemployment at a two-year low of 6.4%, but Statistics Canada's July advance estimate was 0.0% and that reading predates both the 22 August US duties and the 8 September Canadian counter-measures. The euro area grew 0.4% quarter on quarter with the German Ifo at 88.8 against an 87.2 forecast, the flash composite PMI at 52.1 with new orders at a 40-month high, and German manufacturing at 54.1. Net tactical read: a modest pair-bullish tilt on the inflation composition, held to 55 because Canada's activity momentum is the stronger of the two in the data already published.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: The strategic growth differential is the clearest macro divergence in the pair, and it opens rather than closes. The Bank of Canada's own July projection has Canadian GDP at just 0.7% for 2026 as a whole, which after a 3.3% annualised Q2 implies materially sub-trend second-half outcomes even before tariff drag is added; the July advance estimate of 0.0% is the first datapoint consistent with that path. Against it the euro area is stabilising at roughly 1.0% year on year with a multi-year domestic demand floor from German fiscal expansion - a EUR500bn infrastructure fund, defence at approximately 2.8% of GDP in 2026 rising toward 3.5% by 2029, total investment including special funds of EUR126.7bn up 10% on 2025 - which is already visible in German manufacturing at 54.1. Canada has no comparable offset and carries a household sector that cannot absorb tightening: debt to disposable income at 179.6%, mortgage delinquency balances up 32% year on year, and consumer insolvencies at their highest since 2009. On inflation both converge down, but from different compositions and to different policy conclusions. Canadian headline converges toward its 2.0% core as the gasoline base effect rolls off through Q4 and Q1, which removes the statistical basis for the market's Canadian hike pricing. Euro-area headline also decays as energy base effects approach, but from a core of 2.5% with services at 3.3%, so the ECB retains a reason to have tightened even as the terminal drifts. The transmission to the pair is through the reaction functions rather than through relative demand. Confidence 58 rather than higher because the euro area's own improvement is narrow - French Q2 GDP was 0.0% with a composite PMI at 48.8 and German services at 48.5.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: EUR/CAD is the lowest-beta risk cross available in either dossier's complex - neither leg is a haven, both are mid-carry, and the two risk sensitivities very nearly cancel by construction. Holding a 0.05 weight on a factor whose bilateral netting is structurally near zero over six months overstates its information content; the released weight goes to Factor 5, where the bilateral asymmetry is genuine.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is the pair in which the risk factor most nearly cancels, and Neutral is a conclusion rather than a default. Neither currency is a safe haven and neither is a pure risk proxy: the euro is a mid-carry non-haven that performs best in the risk-neutral zone where the dollar loses its precautionary bid, and the Canadian dollar carries a mild positive risk beta that the base dossier's own framework puts at roughly half the Antipodean sensitivity because the US economic linkage anchors it. The regime is unambiguously supportive of both: the VIX closed at 14.51 on 27 August, down 3.70 points on the month after touching a 2026 low of 14.2, US investment-grade spreads are 79bp and high yield 263bp with the latter 21bp tighter, the Euro Stoxx 50 set a record above 6,560 and the S&P 500 stands near 7,670 up roughly 16% year to date. The cross-check that matters is that both dossiers independently scored this factor Bullish tactically at the same 55 confidence for the same reasons, which is the definition of a cancelling bilateral. Two second-order asymmetries partially offset each other. The euro benefits from a falling broad dollar through the anti-dollar channel; the Canadian dollar benefits from the oil complex, with Brent back above $90 on 31 August. Pointing the other way, the TSX fell 1.02% on 31 August even as global indices held, a tariff-specific Canadian equity drag the euro area does not carry.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk factor becomes a distribution question rather than a level question, and for this specific cross the distribution is close to symmetric. A volatility shock from a 2026-low VIX would hurt the euro against the dollar, franc and yen, but the Canadian dollar is not one of those three - it is a mid-beta cyclical with a commodity leg, so a risk-off episode damages both legs of EUR/CAD rather than one. That symmetry is the whole finding. Two further considerations offset. Constructive for the euro leg: European equity leadership reflects earnings and fiscal stimulus rather than pure multiple expansion. Constructive for the Canadian leg: the AI capital-expenditure cycle shows no sign of stalling, and credit is tightening rather than widening. The one asymmetry worth naming is that the oil and risk channels have decoupled: the current oil strength is a supply constraint from a contested Strait of Hormuz, not a demand signal, so it raises Canadian revenue while suppressing the global growth Canadian exports serve - removing the Canadian dollar's usual risk beta and pushing the netting even closer to zero. Both dossiers independently reached Neutral strategically on this factor, at 55 and 50 confidence respectively.

net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the framework's direction rules leg by leg. Oil up: EUR gets a single negative as a large net importer, CAD gets a double positive as an exporter - net effect is the pair FALLS, bearish EUR/CAD. TTF gas up: EUR gets a double negative because gas is its critical import and the 2022 precedent established the transmission, while CAD is at worst neutral and at the margin a beneficiary as a competing hydrocarbon producer - net effect is the pair FALLS, bearish EUR/CAD, and by more than the oil channel alone. Both live commodity channels therefore push the same direction, which is unusual: most commodity crosses have at least one offsetting leg. The pair carries a compounded bearish commodity exposure with no internal hedge, and the only structural offset in the entire factor is the euro area's $16.9bn bilateral goods surplus with Canada, which is a level rather than a rate of change and is roughly one twentieth the size of the annual deterioration in the euro area's aggregate goods surplus.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The two central banks are communicating in opposite registers and that divergence is the pair-relevant fact. The ECB's Account of the 22-23 July meeting, published 27 August, twice described the hold as a pause, stated explicitly that it was important not to suggest the tightening cycle had ended, and judged that a further increase would likely be necessary unless the inflation outlook improved significantly - optionality-preserving hawkishness that the market received exactly as intended, moving September pricing to roughly 97% within days. Executive Board member Schnabel has been delivering what BNY characterises as extremely hawkish messaging. The Bank of Canada is doing the reverse on purpose: its July statement judged the current rate appropriate while adding that uncertainty is still high, and the published Summary of Deliberations records a Council that agreed to look through the direct effects of higher global oil prices because there was limited evidence of spillover, while simultaneously agreeing to reiterate that it would not let higher oil prices lead to persistent inflation - a hawkish commitment device bolted onto a dovish assessment. That Summary also discloses an explicit range of views among Governing Council members on the sustainability of the rebound, which reduces the informational value of any single meeting's tone. Sequence matters and it favours the euro inside the window: the Bank of Canada decided on 2026-09-02 with nothing to say, and the ECB follows on 2026-09-10 with a full projections round at which upward revisions to the June baseline of 3.0% for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027 are likely given energy at +10.0%.

Ottawa's own assessment is that no substantive talks resume before the 2026-11-03 midterms, Carney told premiers that industry support would remain in place beyond the life of the current US administration, and one premier put the planning horizon at two years. The escalation is already announced and dated: US tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel rise to 50% on 2027-01-01, striking the very sector whose 27.0% export surge drove Canada's Q2 growth. The USMCA architecture that would normally constrain this was dismantled when the mandatory six-year review was triggered on 2026-07-01, with US-Mexico bilateral talks proceeding on a separate track and Canada absent from it. The base leg's structural event risk is real but smaller and partly self-cancelling: a Gulf escalation is euro-negative through gas and terms of trade, but a durable ceasefire and Hormuz reopening would be euro-positive on terms of trade while simultaneously removing Canada's oil revenue - so the Gulf branch is genuinely two-sided for this cross in a way the tariff branch is not. What remains one-sidedly euro-negative is France.

What is priced versus what we expect: the market prices the euro path roughly right, prices a Canadian hike it will not get, prices no discount for a European winter energy squeeze, and prices the Canadian tariff regime as a negotiation having a bad quarter rather than a two-year structural condition. Three of those four errors are pair-bullish and the largest single one is not. Conviction is 2 because a Bullish produced by two large cancelling forces is less stable than one produced by breadth: either force winning decisively would move this cross materially in its direction, and it is the lowest-drift, zero-carry pair in either complex with a -34.2bp funding headwind against the position.
strategic.g10_relative_ranking: Strategically EUR/CAD ranks as the most direct available expression of the euro's fourth-of-eleven standing against Canada's seventh-of-eleven, and it is the only cross in either complex where that comparison is unpolluted by a rates overlay. It ranks behind a long EUR/CHF, which captures the euro's rate advantage while collecting 225bp widening to 275bp rather than paying 34bp, and behind a short CAD/NOK. It ranks well ahead of EUR/NOK and EUR/AUD, and ahead of EUR/USD, where six months of negative carry are not covered by the base dossier's own expected path. Among Canadian crosses a long EUR/CAD is the cleanest short-Canada vehicle for anyone who wants to avoid USD/CAD, where 131,035 contracts of speculative short are already concentrated - EUR/CAD does not carry that crowding risk.

Meanwhile the consensus is not discounting that the Bank of Canada publishes its decisive forecast round on 2026-10-28, one day before the ECB and seven weeks before the ECB's own downward test on 2026-12-17 - the Canadian repricing has the earlier venue. cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: The stance labels differ but the scores are only 0.0040 apart in magnitude, so two things are true at once: the label difference is largely a threshold artefact (+0.0986 and +0.1026 straddle the +0.10 boundary by fourteen and twenty-six ten-thousandths respectively), yet underneath that coincidence the composition genuinely changes. Policy and Rates goes from contributing exactly zero to contributing +0.1320 because a 0bp differential with both September decisions at 97% priced is worthless over four weeks, while the travel from 0bp toward +25bp or +50bp is real over two quarters. External Balance goes from -0.0540 to -0.1254 as its weight rises from 0.09 to 0.19 and confidence from 60 to 66. Inflation and Growth stays Bullish but changes its evidence entirely, and Guidance stays Bullish but relocates its venue.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: Late October 2026, specifically the two-day cluster of the Bank of Canada decision with Monetary Policy Report on 2026-10-28 followed by the ECB decision on 2026-10-29 - the first scheduled venue at which the Canadian hike premium can be marked down against a full forecast round, with Canada going first by one day. The secondary inflection is physical rather than scheduled: the autumn European gas injection season, where storage entering November nearer 75% or 85% against the 62.99% recorded on 24 August determines whether Factor 5's -0.1254 grows or shrinks.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Do not carry the strategic view at full weight through the tactical window. The tactical Neutral is the specific observation that the rates channel contributes nothing while both September decisions are 97% priced, and that the two forces which do carry information over four weeks - energy terms of trade and relative positioning crowding - both run against the strategic direction. The disciplined approach is to hold minimal directional spot exposure into 2026-09-16, treat any test of 1.5980-1.6000 as scale-in territory, and add the balance of the strategic position after the 2026-10-28 Monetary Policy Report either confirms the thesis or removes its largest positive contribution.

catalysts.event: Bank of Canada policy decision, statement and press conference
catalysts.rationale: The decision itself carried no pair information - bond markets priced a 3% hike probability and all 35 Reuters-polled economists forecast a hold, leaving the bilateral policy differential at exactly 0bp going into the ECB's own meeting eight days later. The tradeable content was the press-conference tone. This date falls between the valuation date and the payload's spot date; the price series shows EUR/CAD fell 67 pips on the session with a 113-pip range, the widest in a month, but the policy outcome itself is not asserted in this analysis's evidence set.

catalysts.event: Canada merchandise trade balance (July); euro-area final composite and services PMIs and producer prices
catalysts.rationale: Both legs report on the same day and the quote leg has the greater surprise potential. Canada's trade consensus of C$3.2bn sits below the C$3.86bn prior, implying the market expects immediate tariff drag on data that predates the 2026-08-22 Section 338 duties entirely. A beat extends the record-export run that produced a twenty-one-year-high current account and is pair-bearish through Factor 5. The euro-area final PMIs test whether the flash composite at 52.1 with new orders at a 40-month high holds on revision.

catalysts.event: Canada Labour Force Survey (August) and Ivey PMI; euro-area retail sales and German factory orders; ECB Chief Economist Lane before the quiet period; CFTC Commitments of Traders
catalysts.rationale: The Canadian employment consensus of +15.8k follows July's +75.1k and a third consecutive decline in unemployment to a two-year low of 6.4%, so the bar is materially lowered and a beat would extend the hawkish Canadian repricing that is pair-bearish. Lane's remarks are the last significant ECB communication before the quiet period and the most likely vehicle for a late steer on the 2026-09-10 decision. The positioning print is the first read on whether either of the two simultaneous short-covering runs has continued, which matters for the proportional netting in Factor 4.

catalysts.event: Canada's retaliatory tariffs take effect on approximately US$20bn of US goods at 15-50%
catalysts.rationale: Targets include US steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, electronics and motorcycles, and the product-level list was unpublished at the valuation date, so the market cannot have priced its composition. Carney called the step reluctant precisely because it raises Canadian costs and reduces choice, and dollar-for-dollar retaliation by an economy roughly one tenth the size is proportionally heavier on Canada. The transmission is a one-sided quote-leg growth and cost shock with no base-leg equivalent, since the euro area settled its own trade dispute at a 15% framework live from 1 July. This is the largest gap-risk date in the tactical window and the pair's flat volatility surface prices none of it.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections
catalysts.rationale: The mechanical event of the tactical window: a 25bp move to a 2.50% deposit rate is roughly 97% priced and would open the pair's first positive policy differential, taking it from exactly 0bp to +25bp in the euro's favour against a Bank of Canada that has just held. Because the decision is discounted, the pair-relevant content is the projection revisions to the June baseline of 3.0% headline for 2026 and 2.3% for 2027, which energy at +10.0% year on year makes likely to be revised up. The tonal risk is that Lagarde repeats the July acknowledgement that there is no clear evidence of second-round effects, which would produce the classic spike-and-fade around the 50-day at 1.61219.

catalysts.event: Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index for August
catalysts.rationale: The highest-information quote-leg release of the tactical window and genuinely two-sided for the pair. Priors are headline 3.0%, CPI-trim 1.9%, CPI-median 2.0% and CPI-common 2.7%. If CPI-trim rises toward 2.2-2.5% the oil-broadening the Bank said it would respond to becomes live, the market's Canadian hike pricing is validated rather than faded, and the pair's largest strategic positive is undermined. If trim slips at or below 1.9% the statistical basis for a 2026 hike disappears and the Factor 1 and Factor 6 theses are confirmed seven weeks before their scheduled test.

catalysts.event: Federal Open Market Committee decision with Summary of Economic Projections
catalysts.rationale: Not a decision about either leg, but it reaches the cross asymmetrically, which is the entire content of Factor 10. Roughly 58-60% of a 25bp hike is priced after Chair Warsh's 28 August Jackson Hole address moved odds from 36%. A hawkish outcome lifts Bund yields in sympathy - already at a fifteen-year high of 3.29-3.30% with the UST-Bund spread narrowed to roughly 138bp - while the Bank of Canada has stated that Canadian yields were little changed as US yields rose, so the base leg's curve co-moves and the quote leg's lags. That transmission is pair-bullish; the offsetting risk is a broad-dollar bid that pressures both legs.

catalysts.event: Statistics Canada Consumer Price Index for September (approximate, monthly release)
catalysts.rationale: The first Canadian print in which the gasoline base effect turns materially less favourable and the first capable of capturing tariff pass-through in both directions - US duties raising Canadian export costs and Canadian counter-duties raising import prices. Headline converging down toward the 2.0% core average removes the statistical support for the market's roughly 65% probability of a 2026 Bank of Canada hike, which is the single largest support under the quote currency and therefore the largest identified pair-bullish repricing available. It lands eight days before the Monetary Policy Report that would formalise it.

catalysts.event: Bank of Canada decision with Monetary Policy Report
catalysts.rationale: The pivotal scheduled event of the strategic horizon and the identified cross-horizon inflection. The Bank must publish a full forecast round incorporating the first post-tariff activity data, marking down 2026 growth for the tariff shock while marking down inflation as the gasoline base effect rolls off - the combination that removes the analytical basis for a 2026 hike and reprices the front end that currently supports the quote currency. National Bank and Scotiabank forecast a hike to 2.50% here, which would invalidate rather than confirm the thesis; the other four large Canadian banks forecast a hold. It falls one day before the ECB, so Canada sets the tone for the cross.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision (no staff projections)
catalysts.rationale: A non-projection meeting arriving one day after the Bank of Canada's full forecast round, so the pair will already have repriced on the quote leg before the base leg speaks. The base case is a hold at a delivered 2.50%, which means the language matters more than the decision: a hold framed as another pause sustains the terminal that the euro's rate-of-change case depends on, while a hold framed as data-dependent with softening wage commentary begins the 15-25bp downward repricing that is the base leg's own principal risk.

The only dated circuit-breaker for the Canadian tariff regime inside the strategic horizon, and therefore the largest single risk to the pair-bullish Event Risk contribution. Ottawa's own assessment is that no substantive talks resume before this date, and the mechanism by which the midterms would help is US domestic pressure from tariff-driven cost-of-living pain - American consumers absorbed more than US$231bn in tariff costs between February 2025 and January 2026, roughly US$1,745 per family. A credible negotiation restart would reprice the entire Canadian tariff premium at once rather than gradually.

catalysts.event: Northern-hemisphere heating season begins in earnest: the physical test of the 62.99% EU gas storage level recorded 24 August (week-of marker, not a scheduled release)
catalysts.rationale: The highest-information event of the strategic horizon for the base leg and the one force capable of overturning the pair verdict without any central bank acting. EU storage at 62.99% on 24 August was well below historical averages against an effectively closed Strait of Hormuz carrying almost a fifth of global LNG trade, and Goldman Sachs has said current prices will not be enough for Europe to manage storage through winter with December TTF possibly needing to exceed EUR100/MWh. Every increment on TTF is a direct debit to the euro-area goods surplus and, in this cross, a direct credit to a Canadian dollar whose energy exports are tariff-exempt.

catalysts.event: Bank of Canada decision (fixed announcement date, no projection round)
catalysts.rationale: The terminal date for the market's roughly 65% probability of a 2026 Canadian hike. National Bank and Scotiabank forecast 2.75% by this meeting; the other four large Canadian banks forecast no change. If the Bank has not moved by this date the entire 2026 hike premium is removed from the Canadian curve, which is worth an estimated 15-20bp on the two-year and is the mechanism by which the pair's largest strategic positive is realised. It precedes the ECB's December projections round by eight days.

catalysts.event: ECB Governing Council decision with new Eurosystem staff macroeconomic projections
catalysts.rationale: The base leg's own downward test, and the reason the pair's Guidance factor is Bullish at only 52 confidence. This is the projection vintage in which 2026 energy base effects first come clearly into the 2027 and 2028 forecast window; a downward revision to the 2027 path removes the justification for the market's 2.75% terminal and reprices the euro strip lower, offsetting the Canadian repricing expected seven weeks earlier.

catalysts.event: United States tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, automotive parts and steel rise to 50%
catalysts.rationale: A dated, pre-announced escalation that extends the Canadian tariff regime well beyond the current US$20bn and 5.2% of bilateral exports, and strikes precisely the sector whose 27.0% annualised export surge drove Canada's Q2 GDP. Section 338 carries no expiry, so the escalation persists until a presidential proclamation removes it, and the Bank of Canada estimates approximately 2 million Canadian jobs depend on goods exports to the United States.

assumptions: Direction provenance: this is pass 2 of 2. The ten factor stances, confidences, evidence types, applied weights, weighted contributions, net scores, convictions, rationales, G10 rankings and cross-horizon assessment are carried unchanged from the settled Direction Verdict, which was scored without the price payload by design. Everything price-derived (Market Context, Bilateral Carry Analysis, scenarios, targets, path expectation, conviction ladders, risk/reward, forward-versus-spot, invalidator levels and signpost thresholds) is this pass's own work.

Price payload provenance: the gated append-only store delivered 130 data points spanning 2026-03-06 to 2026-09-03, with spot 1.60356 at spotDate 2026-09-03 and 0 weekend bars dropped. Data-quality notes disclose that only 2 resistance and 7 support zones met the 2-touch threshold, and that moving averages, zones, 52-week range, performance figures and 200-week statistics are computed over the whole stored history from 2008-08-26 (4,697 weekday bars), not over the 130 bars shown.

Spot date versus valuation date: the payload's spotDate of 2026-09-03 is two trading days after the 2026-09-01 valuation date. The 2026-09-02 Bank of Canada decision falls inside that gap; its price effect (a 67-pip decline on a 113-pip range) is described as price action, but the policy outcome itself was not in pass 1's evidence set and is not asserted anywhere in this report.

Moving-average basis: all moving averages are simple averages of trading-day closes on a weekday-only series. The 200-week average at 1.51972 with a slope of +0.001558 per week is treated as a first-class structural level given spot has closed above it every recorded week.

Volatility provenance and known bias: EUR/CAD has no listed option; implied volatilities are triangle realised-correlation estimates at implied correlation 0.7331, not quotes, and the payload's own back-check found the method understating direct Eurex quotes by 8.7-17.8% (14.4% median across seventeen pairs). Every quoted implied level is treated as a floor. No IV percentile, 25-delta risk reversal or butterfly exists for this cross.

Carry and forward derivation: the policy differential is exactly 0bp. The -34.2bp annualised roll premium is the listed-futures roll (interest differential plus cross-currency basis) and is never reported as a policy differential. Forward outrights are derived by applying that premium linearly to spot; no quoted forward points for this cross were available.

Rate block basis: both 10-year yields in the payload are monthly series as of 2026-06-01 and are never quoted as live levels; the computed differential is corroborated by live 31 August levels each dossier carries independently.

Support and resistance methodology: zones are taken exactly as computed by the payload from clustered weekly and monthly swing closes, ranked by touch count rather than proximity; the payload's disclosure of a resistance shortfall (2 zones vs 7 support zones) is honoured rather than concealed. No web-sourced support or resistance level is used anywhere.

Bilateral trade: IMF DOTS goods only, 2024 annual, used exactly as supplied without re-estimation; the $16.9bn euro-area net goods surplus with Canada excludes services, investment income and portfolio flows and is weighed as a level rather than a rate of change.

Bilateral web research limits: forecast sources located are aggregator compilations rather than primary bank research and are treated as best-available; no pair-specific option barrier data, risk reversal, vol surface or cross-currency basis for EUR/CAD could be sourced and each is recorded as a documented gap. Extrapolation-script forecast sites were deliberately excluded from the citation list as a category error rather than evidence.

Bilateral investment flows: no quantified EU-Canada portfolio or FDI flow series was sourced; the qualitative CETA investment-regime development is structurally relevant but is a multi-year dynamic with no dated trigger inside either horizon and is not scored.

Probability estimates: all scenario probabilities, invalidator probabilities and tail assessments are structured judgements, not market-implied figures; each scenario set sums to 100%. The roughly 25% probability assigned to a 2026 Bank of Canada hike against a market-implied 65% is inherited from the quote dossier and is labelled at each point of use.

Citation numbering: citations 1-29 are inherited from the direction verdict's own verified reference list carrying 2026-09-01 access dates; citations 30 and above are new to this pass and were accessed on 2026-09-04.
